components.name: Tonal Button
components.description: A secondary action, such as Paste lyrics or Sync now.

narrative.overview: A dark room with one light on what matters. Songbook's page is nearly black, and the only things lit are the song you are about to play and the controls you can press. The library is plain lines in the dark; the song you played last is the one lit card at the top; the lyrics, once open, are the brightest and largest thing on the screen. The mood is quietly confident, with one violet accent marking what you can act on.
keyCharacteristics: A nearly black page; depth comes from stepping between greys and from one lit card, not from shadows.
One violet accent, on actions and the current state only.
One 16px corner on everything except the round add button and switch.
Large, calm type for lyrics; small, quiet type for everything around them.
Controls move out of the way while reading, and full screen leaves only the way back.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The accent marks what can be pressed or what is current. If a screen has more than a handful of accent elements, something that should be grey has been coloured.

rules.name: The Step-Down Rule
rules.body: Each layer is one grey step from the one behind it: Stage Black, then Control Grey, then Well Grey. Tags and tonal buttons sit below the surface they are on, not above it. The only lit surface on a list screen is the song that is about to be played.

rules.name: The Words First Rule
rules.body: The lyric is the largest and brightest text on any screen it appears on. Nothing around it is larger or higher in contrast.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow appears only on something that floats above the page (a menu, a thumb), never to make a card look raised.

dos: Do keep the page Stage Black and light only the song you are about to play (the last-played card) and what can be pressed.
Do use Violet Signal only for things you can act on or the current state.
Do use the 16px corner everywhere, and fully round shapes only for circular buttons and the switch.
Do keep touch targets at 44px or larger, and put frequent actions in the lower half of the screen.
Do let controls leave the screen while the song is being read.
Do keep the phone, web and desktop versions looking the same.
donts: Don't add shadows to cards or buttons to make them look raised.
Don't put library songs back on grey cards: the list is plain lines in the dark.
Don't introduce a second accent colour next to the chosen one.
Don't make any text on a song screen larger or higher in contrast than the lyrics.
Don't put an action behind a gesture alone: every swipe or double tap needs an on-screen route.
Don't load web fonts or add a second font family; the device's own font is the system.
